classification: dirty-tree native unit/integration diagnostic; not signed qualification
changes: Realm descriptors and canonical security-token handles now belong to isolate-owned NativeRealmIdentities.
Initial and subsequent driver-created contexts use one scope-based native realm factory.
The factory can run inside a native callback without borrowing the host driver or retaining an unsafe host pointer.
Failed environment allocation removes the newly registered realm while preserving monotonic identity allocation.

new_test_assertions: Native realm and generated Document bindings can be created during an active JavaScript callback.
The caller context is restored after child binding installation.
The child has distinct JavaScript intrinsics and a usable native Document in the same script turn.
An opaque-origin child denies parent document access.
Retained child Document access survives low-memory garbage collection.

qualification_boundary: No new signed build or WPT result is claimed. The prior signed frame-disposal candidate is preserved separately.
next_required_integration: Register callback-created contexts and bindings with the document driver through native coordinator state.
Create and link the initial about:blank Document and Window synchronously at connected iframe insertion.
Apply inherited origin, base URL and sandbox policy before exposing the initial context.
Retain or replace the initial Window and Document according to navigation rules, with native stable WindowProxy ownership.
Cover same-turn access, nested insertion, removal, navigation, sandboxing and initial-document identity in native and upstream tests.
